# Encoding and decoding strategy

This vignette describes the current class metadata and encoding components. The
save and restore entry points are still being integrated with the class factories.

## Class declarations

`RSObjectClass()` creates object class generators, `RSProtocolClass()` creates
protocol declarations, and `RSSingletonClass()` creates a shared instance when
the class is declared. Singleton generators store that instance in `$instance`
and `robjc_isa$slot`. `RSScalarClass()` sets `isNAClass` before creating a
singleton scalar such as `RSNull`.

The factories attach `robjc_isa` to each generator and set the same metadata
reference in the R6 private fields. The metadata contains the superclass,
protocols, version, and optional singleton slot. Class and protocol identity is
therefore based on generator references rather than class-name strings alone.

## Encoding metadata

`RSClassEncoder` is declared with `RSSingletonClass()` and implements
`RSEncoderProtocol`. Its `encodeObject()` method traverses objects implementing
`RSEncoding`; `objectsForEncoding()` supplies child objects. A visited-object
environment prevents repeated traversal. `lockInstance()` finalizes a dictionary
of `RSClassReference` entries, each holding an `RSInstanceMap` for a class ID.

`RSWrappedClass` combines a generator's name and `robjc_isa$version` into a
class ID. The identifier is stored as an `RSString`. `RSClassRegistry` collects
the framework class names used during class resolution.

## Native collection storage

Dictionary and set wrappers delegate storage to `RSConcreteDictionary` and
`RSConcreteSet`. These adapters hold Rcpp external pointers to the native
tables. The native tables call the stored objects' `hash()` and `isEqual()`
methods. Before serialization, `prepareForSerialization()` records R-side
snapshots so the adapters can rebuild native storage after deserialization.

## Decoding metadata

`RSClassDecoder` reads the encoded class references and resolves class IDs
against runtime generators. `resolveClassWith()` replaces an object's private
`.__isa` reference. It does not recreate the R6 instance's methods or fields.
Unresolved class IDs are recorded in the decoder's `unresolved` field.

## Current I/O integration

The factories expose singleton instances as `$instance`, and the public
`robjc_save*()` and `robjc_read_rds()`/`robjc_load()` entry points use that
accessor. Restoring an object against a changed class definition remains
unresolved: `resolveClassWith()` updates class metadata, but does not rebuild
the R6 instance's methods or fields.

## Example: encode, save, and read

The following example first inspects the encoded metadata, then saves the
object and reads the RDS payload. `robjc_save_rds()` performs its own encoding,
so the manual encoding step is for inspection.

```{r}
library(robjc)

obj <- RSString_withValue("hello")
encoder <- RSClassEncoder$instance$refresh()
encoder$encodeObject(obj)
metadata <- encoder$lockInstance()
stopifnot(metadata$count() > 0L)

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
robjc_save_rds(obj, path)
payload <- readRDS(path)
stopifnot(all(c("__object__", "__robjc__") %in% names(payload)))
loaded <- payload[["__object__"]]
stopifnot(identical(loaded$value(), "hello"))
unlink(path)
```

`readRDS()` reads the serialized object and metadata as they were stored; it
does not resolve saved class definitions against the current runtime. Full
class-aware restoration through `robjc_read_rds()` is still under development;
it currently fails for this `RSString` example. Restoration after a class
definition changes also remains unresolved.
